$comment: IaC compare: the same resource in ARM JSON, Bicep and Terraform (azurerm 4.x). Each concept lists substrings that mark its lines in each language.

resources.title: Storage account
resources.summary: A hardened StorageV2 account: TLS 1.2, HTTPS only, no anonymous blob access.
resources.terraform:
variable "storage_name" {
  type = string
}

resource "azurerm_storage_account" "storage" {
  name                            = var.storage_name
  resource_group_name             = azurerm_resource_group.rg.name
  location                        = azurerm_resource_group.rg.location
  account_tier                    = "Standard"
  account_replication_type        = "LRS"
  account_kind                    = "StorageV2"
  access_tier                     = "Hot"
  min_tls_version                 = "TLS1_2"
  allow_nested_items_to_be_public = false
  https_traffic_only_enabled      = true
}

concepts.label: Resource type and version
concepts.note: ARM and Bicep name the Azure resource provider type and pin an API version; Terraform uses the azurerm provider's resource name, and the version is the provider version (in required_providers).

concepts.label: Inputs
concepts.note: ARM parameters are JSON objects referenced with [parameters('x')]; Bicep has param; Terraform has variable blocks referenced as var.x.

concepts.label: Location and resource group
concepts.note: ARM/Bicep deploy into the resource group of the deployment, so only location is set (defaulting to the group's). Terraform must name the resource group explicitly.

concepts.label: SKU and redundancy
concepts.note: One SKU name in ARM/Bicep (Standard_LRS); Terraform splits it into account_tier and account_replication_type.

concepts.label: Kind and access tier
concepts.note: Same values, different casing: camelCase properties in ARM/Bicep, snake_case attributes in Terraform.

concepts.label: Minimum TLS
concepts.note: minimumTlsVersion vs min_tls_version - same setting.

concepts.label: Anonymous blob access
concepts.note: allowBlobPublicAccess in the REST API is allow_nested_items_to_be_public in azurerm - the naming most often trips people up.

concepts.label: HTTPS only
concepts.note: supportsHttpsTrafficOnly vs https_traffic_only_enabled (named enable_https_traffic_only before azurerm 4.0).

resources.title: Virtual network with a subnet
resources.summary: A VNet with one subnet - inline in ARM/Bicep, a separate resource in Terraform.

concepts.label: Resource type and version
concepts.note: Network resources have their own frequent API versions in ARM/Bicep; Terraform pins the provider instead.

concepts.label: Address space
concepts.note: An object with addressPrefixes in ARM/Bicep; a plain list in Terraform.

concepts.label: Subnets
concepts.note: Inline in the VNet in ARM/Bicep. Terraform's azurerm_subnet is a separate resource - don't mix inline subnet blocks and azurerm_subnet for the same VNet, or they fight on every apply.

concepts.label: Dependencies
concepts.note: Inline subnets need no dependency. Terraform infers order from the reference to azurerm_virtual_network.vnet.name; in ARM a separate subnet resource would need dependsOn.

concepts.label: Outputs
concepts.note: Bicep and Terraform make returning an ID easy; in ARM you'd add an outputs section with reference() or resourceId().

resources.title: App Service plan and Linux web app
resources.summary: A B1 Linux plan with a Node.js web app: HTTPS only, TLS 1.2, FTPS off, managed identity.

concepts.label: The plan
concepts.note: serverfarms is the API name for an App Service plan. Terraform calls it azurerm_service_plan.

concepts.label: Linux
concepts.note: A quirk of the API: a Linux plan is kind 'linux' plus reserved: true. Terraform says os_type = "Linux" and uses a separate azurerm_linux_web_app resource.

concepts.label: Linking app to plan
concepts.note: ARM needs resourceId() plus dependsOn; Bicep's plan.id creates the dependency implicitly; Terraform's reference does the same.

concepts.label: Runtime stack
concepts.note: linuxFxVersion 'NODE|20-lts' in ARM/Bicep; an application_stack block in Terraform.

concepts.label: HTTPS, TLS and FTPS
concepts.note: Same three settings, different names: httpsOnly/https_only, minTlsVersion/minimum_tls_version, ftpsState/ftps_state.

concepts.label: Managed identity
concepts.note: An identity object in ARM/Bicep; an identity block in Terraform.

concepts.label: Names from inputs
concepts.note: concat() in ARM, string interpolation '${}' in Bicep and Terraform.

resources.title: Key Vault
resources.summary: An RBAC-mode vault with purge protection and public network access disabled.

concepts.label: Tenant
concepts.note: ARM/Bicep read it from subscription().tenantId; Terraform reads it from the azurerm_client_config data source.

concepts.label: SKU
concepts.note: An object with family 'A' and a name in ARM/Bicep; just sku_name in Terraform.

concepts.label: Permission model
concepts.note: enableRbacAuthorization: true switches from access policies to Azure RBAC. Terraform: enable_rbac_authorization - newer azurerm 4.x releases rename it rbac_authorization_enabled, so check your provider version.

concepts.label: Soft delete
concepts.note: Soft delete is always on now. ARM/Bicep still show enableSoftDelete; Terraform has no switch, only the retention days.

concepts.label: Purge protection
concepts.note: Once on, it cannot be turned off - deleted vaults stay recoverable for the retention period.

concepts.label: Public network access
concepts.note: 'Disabled' string in ARM/Bicep vs a boolean in Terraform - reach it through a private endpoint.
